dedupe_keys.name: disaster storylines and knowledge graphs from global news with large language models and retrieval augmented generation

description: Disaster Storylines and Knowledge Graphs from Global News with Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Michele Ronco et al. We present a dataset of over 3,000 global disaster events from 2014 to 2024, derived from the Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT). Events are extracted from news using a pipeline combining Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for semantic extraction. The corpus is the Europe Media Monitor (EMM), aggregating content from millions of news outlets. Coverage: global; published in 2026. Formats: CSV. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
